I've owned my 2005 Cobalt since new. It appears that a wheel bearing is going out.. going to have it repaired by a mechanic next week. Is it a good idea to have these replaces in pairs, or is that a waste of money?

For instance, if it's the LF that is bad, should I replace LF + RF? Thanks.
Wheel bearing advice [05 Chevy Cobalt LS]

You can just have one side replaced, but since both wheel bearings are the same age and have been operated under the same conditions odds are that the one on the other side does not have much life left in it. I always recommend to my customers that they replace both sides if one fails at this age, but that does double the repair cost and therefore it does not always fit into everyone's monthly budget.

You may want to request that the mechanic install a top quality hub & bearing assembly, such as an AC-Delco brand. Most parts manufacturers make both a good quality line of parts that are equivalent to the original ones (which have lasted 10 years, right)? and also a cheaper discount line of the same brand of parts, often of questionable quality, that they sell at lower prices to compete with other discount parts suppliers. In general the slightly costlier top quality parts will last much longer than the cheap ones from discount parts suppliers, and have a much longer warranty.

There are actually three different part numbers of GM front hub & bearing assemblies for this year Cobalt, depending on whether you have ABS and/ or rear disc brakes. They range in price between about $225 and $250 for the part, and GM's flat rate labor time to replace both sides is 1.3 hours.
Thanks, I'll replace the pair and keep an eye on the part selection that is offered.
